privacy: Files and text stay in your browser. Nothing is uploaded or saved.
dropHelp: Drop a text file here or choose one, such as TXT, CSV, JSON or SRT.
sourceHelp: If the preview looks garbled, choose the encoding used to save the original file.
textPlaceholder: Paste text to save in another encoding…
textHelp: Pasted text is already Unicode. Source encoding applies only to files.
sourceUnknown: This file is not valid UTF-8 and has no recognized BOM. Choose its source encoding and check the preview.
invalidBytes: Some bytes are invalid in this source encoding. Choose another source encoding or use an undamaged original file. Download is blocked to avoid losing text.
binary: This input contains binary control characters. Choose a text file and check its source encoding.
unsupportedBom: This file has a UTF-32 BOM. UTF-32 is not supported; save the original file as UTF-8 or UTF-16 first.
bomMismatch: The source encoding conflicts with the file's BOM. Choose Auto or the encoding indicated by the BOM.
unrepresentable: The target encoding cannot preserve every character. The output preview shows the changes. Choose UTF-8 or another compatible encoding to download without losing text.
processingError: The browser could not complete the conversion. Try again or use a smaller file if browser memory is exhausted.
compareHelp: Choose the preview that reads correctly. Valid bytes alone do not prove which encoding was used.
bomHelp: UTF-8 usually needs no BOM. Add one if the receiving app requires it, for example some Excel workflows.
unicodeOnly: BOM is available only for UTF-8 and UTF-16. This encoding is saved without BOM.
downloadHelp: Download saves the actual encoded bytes. Copying text through the clipboard does not preserve a file's encoding.
emptyDescription: Choose a text file or paste text. Check the decoded preview before downloading.
previewNotice: Previews show up to 12,000 characters. Downloads include the full text.
helpText: Source encoding controls how the original bytes are read; target encoding controls how the download is written. UTF-8 is the recommended target for modern apps. Line-ending changes preserve blank lines and the final newline. Encoding conversion does not translate between Simplified and Traditional Chinese and cannot recover characters already saved as ? or �.
